name: run-the-suite
notes: Run the project suite and report the number. "The tests pass" without a count is a claim; a count is a fact. If you did not run them, say that instead of implying you did.

name: confirm-green
notes: Red suite, or a suite you could not run: stop and say so. Pushing over a failure is how the failure becomes somebody else's.

name: stage-by-name
notes: Name every path. Never `git add -A` or `git add .`: staging by pattern is how a secret, a build artefact or somebody else's half-finished edit gets committed by accident.

name: write-the-subject
notes: <type>(<scope>): <imperative>, 72 characters or fewer, no trailing period. type is feat | fix | refactor | chore | docs | test | perf | style.

name: write-the-body
notes: Why: the problem that triggered this. What for: what becomes possible or true afterwards. Where: the seam it lands in, when the change and its effect live apart — omit it rather than write filler. Never a Co-Authored-By trailer or any signature: the author is the user.

name: checks
notes: Nothing is pushed over a red or unrun suite.

name: push
notes: Ask first, every time. Never --no-verify and never --no-gpg-sign: a hook that fails is a thing to fix, not to bypass. No --amend after a push.

name: confirm-the-base
notes: Check which branch the work starts from and that it is clean. A command or a document that assumes `main` is wrong about this repository if its default is `master` — read it rather than assuming either.

name: create-the-branch
notes: <type>/<what-the-session-is-about>, kebab-case. One branch per session — the set of things the session sets out to do, not one per commit. The point is being able to see what a session did as one unit, and to drop it as one unit if it turns out wrong.

name: merge-back
notes: Merged when the work is verified AND the user has tested it. Those are two conditions, and the second one is not yours to decide.

name: look-at-the-real-state
notes: `git status --short`, and whether the suite was run. Uncommitted work or a red suite: say so FIRST and ask whether to close anyway. The next startup has no way to find out on its own.

name: save-the-observations
notes: Every decision, gotcha and piece of progress not yet saved. Not one note per file touched — what would spare an hour to whoever opens this in three weeks. Anything with a current value rather than a history gets a topic_key, so it updates instead of competing.

name: commit-what-is-ready
notes: Only if the user asks. Closing is an act of memory, not of git.

name: write-the-living-state
notes: `set_project_state` REPLACES: write the whole picture, not a delta. Where the work stands, what is verified and what is not, the concrete next action, and what is already settled so it is not re-litigated.

name: offer-the-team-what-is-theirs
notes: When the project is in an org, `end_session` returns promotionProposals. Print it verbatim, ask, and promote only what the user confirms.

name: end-the-session
notes: summary: one to three retrospective bullets, no celebration. next_session: an ACTION — verb, path or branch, and the command to run. Anything left unverified belongs there; leaving it out is what makes the next session believe it was done.
